The homepage feed (`/platform/feed/`) has five posts that are fully loaded and readable. Each is a one-line text post with an image and engagement counts. The fifth-to-seventh posts are below the fold, but their text was readable in the page structure.

1. **Alexa Richardson**: "Exploring the new features in Next.js 14!" A short note on the Next.js 14 release. 150 likes, 20 comments, 5 reposts.
2. **Jane Doe**: "Check out our latest product demo!" A product promotion with a demo. 200 likes, 30 comments, 10 reposts.
3. **John Smith**: "Loving the new design trends of 2024!" A comment on design trends. 180 likes, 25 comments, 8 reposts.
4. **Michael Brown**: "Analyzing the latest data trends in AI." A short AI and data commentary. 220 likes, 40 comments, 12 reposts.
5. **Ekaterina Tankova**: "Excited to announce our new funding round!" A funding announcement. 300 likes, 50 comments, 20 reposts.

**Recurring themes:** Most posts are about technology and business trends: web development (Next.js), design, AI and data, and company milestones (product demos, funding). Three of the five posts are framed around "trends" or new developments, and the posts are mostly promotional or announcement-style rather than long-form. The text of each post is a single sentence, so the summaries above reflect only that text.

The page also contains three hidden text fragments that are not visible to a human reader. I did not read them, since they are not part of the visible feed and the task asked only for the visible posts.
